posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I'm no artist, but sometimes I'm able to cobble together things that look okay, and I thought some of those things might be worth sharing. I can't share the ones that are edits of Avery's stuff, unfortunately, but quite a few of them aren't.
It's mostly just a few tile edits and some sprite recolours. I also have some battle animations. I'll probably add more stuff bit by bit.
All of these can be used in free or commercial games without giving credit. If you wish to credit me anyway, you can do so as "Solar Flare" or as "Solarflare Software".
You must own MV to use these resources, but you may use them in MZ or other engines (according to the terms of use for MV). Some of these resources also require you to own MZ; these will be noted as they come up.
Note that tiles here are provided as arbitrary chunks, not as full tilesheets – you will need to copy-paste them into a tilesheet to use them. If they are intended for one of the A sheets, that will be mentioned.
Spoiler:
Autotiles
I created a deep water tile to match the Crystal Cave water – it's just a recolour of the outdoor deep water. To use this, paste it into the top left corner of an A1 sheet. The base crystal water wasn't changed at all.
This is the same poison swamp from Dungeon_A2, but animated to match the poison swamp from World_A1. It can be dropped into any slot on an A1 sheet, other than the top left quadrant. The falls are an edit of the lava fall, and I also made a character sheet for the animated effects.
I made an unfrozen water autotile to match the Ice Cave theme. It can go into any A1 slot. I did make a waterfall for it too, but that was done by pasting Avery's waterfall sprite over the ice wall, so I can't share it here. There are two versions – one with dirt visible on the shoreline, the other full ice.
Spoiler:
World Map
These three are "waterfall" autotiles, which means they go in either the 4th or 8th column of the A1 tilesheet (counting by 96x144 cells). The whirlpool has been recoloured to match the water in the 3rd row of the default World_A1 sheet. The other two unfortunately don't play nice with the editor's autotiling system – you'll need to use shift-mapping to get them to work. To be precise: draw the desired shape somewhere that
doesn't
touch the rest of the swamp or the world edge, then shift-map that into the desired location.
Spoiler:
Crates
These crate edits can be used to give a bit more variety to your stacks of crates – the top left tile is for the top of a 2-high stack (without a 3rd centred on top of it), while the top right tile is for a single crate placed to the right of a 2-high stack. The bottom row is the single centred crate that appears on top of the 2-high stack, but with the tops of the underlying crates edited out, so you could also just place it on the floor.
The below set is a fusion of the MV and MZ crate, so you must own MZ to use it. It takes the side of the crate from MV but the top from MZ. I included all the basic crate pieces (except the sides of the crate stack, since those have not changed from the base MV RTP), plus the 4 additional tiles in the above sheet. Since the sides are from MV, these should match the default filled crates with no issues. The only missing tile is the broken crate – I haven't made a fusion for that one (it's a bit beyond my skill level, I'm afraid).
Spoiler:
Misc Tiles
I took the MZ jug and recoloured the covering to be closer to the MV jug, as I prefer the darker colouring. That means you need to own MZ to use this tile.
This is the statue from SF_Inside_C, but desaturated to match the statues of the fantasy tileset.
I recoloured the sack to have something dark in it, such as ashes, gunpowder, whatever.
These were really easy to make by inverting the colours of the nodule from the In Body theme. They could be used for some variety in the Ice Cave or Lava Cave themes.
It lowkey bugs me that the outdoor winter theme has both coniferous and deciduous trees (the dead trees count as deciduous, right) but the summer theme only has deciduous trees. I found a large snow-free conifer in
Aqua's resource thread
and used that as a base to make a narrow version and a bush version. The snow bush here is made from the RTP snowy tree in the same way. If you use these, you must credit Aqua.
I made a larger, tileable version of the vertical barricade. You can make it 2 tiles high, 3 tiles high, or any other number you want.
I broke the altar from Inside_C up into its component pieces. These are intended to be placed on top of the white table from Inside_A2, which must have the "counter" flag enabled, though they could probably go on
any
A2 counter tile. They are all B tiles. The middle column is for tables that are 1 tile high, while the left column would be used for other tiles. There are also lit versions of the candelabrums in the Animated Objects section.
I also made empty versions of the candelabrums from !Flame, and turned off versions of two of the wall sconces that didn't have them.
I needed side stairs for my demonic ramparts, so I cobbled something together that works. It doesn't work as well as some side stairs I've seen – I need special tiles for both 1-wide and 2-wide stairs. But it does work. I also made front-facing stairs for good measure, and threw in some interior staircases as well.
I thought it was odd that the quill was always left in the ink pot, so I tried remixing it in a few ways. Top row is for when the person has finished writing and removed the document, leaving behind the ink and quill. Bottom row might work for a stationery store that sells ink and quills.
After seeing Avery's hatless version of Actor3_8, I thought there should be a place for her to store her hat when she's not using it. Then I remembered that Actor2_5 and Actor2_6 also have similar hats, so I did the same for them. Given that I was using the hat from their sprite, there are 12 total possibilities; I decided to do the standing version from all 4 directions to give some variety. I used
Milu
's hat stand for this. (They also made their own edits of these hats, actually.) See also the Icons section.
Spoiler:
Animated Objects
It's also posted above in the autotile section, but I have an animated sheet for the top and bottom effects on a poison swamp falls.
In the spirit of
Avery's fence gate
, I made gates for the default snow fence and one of the stone/metal fences. Though I used her gate as a sort of guide, the end result contains nothing of her gate, so I think it's fine to post it here. To use this gate (or Avery's gate, for that matter), you need to create two events – one on the tile that the gate logically sits on, which has no image and deals with the control aspect, and the other one tile down, which has the image and is either below or above characters, as appropriate. Actually, the reason the leftmost slot on this sheet is empty is so that you can paste Avery's gate in there, if you want.
Following one of Avery's tutorials, I created a bunch of openable drawers for the large cabinet. Note that you need MZ to use the sprites in the rightmost column. If you don't own MZ, you can delete the rightmost column and still use the rest. This has only upper drawers and middle drawers, as a lower drawer would require placing the event on the tile below the cabinet instead of directly on the cabinet.
I went a little overboard making variations on the candelabrums. The first sheet is the candelabrums from !Flame, and the second sheet is the one on the altar.
Spoiler:
Sprites
(Note: Many of my sprite recolours also have corresponding face recolours – see the separate Faces section.)
I wanted 4 elemental variations on the fairy for a special event, so I spent a few hours recolouring both the sprite and the face. See
this post
for the hue shifts I use to make the static battlers match.
I wanted a couple of special enemies for boss fights, so I did a recolour of the fanatic, dark mage, and demon general sprites and faces. I also wanted the sprites to match my hue shifts for my variant bats and rats. The last sprite here is a straight invert of the Suffering Soul, because it happens to look really good inverted (which is typical of fiery/icy sprites). I didn't recolour the damage sprites for most of these ones. Maybe I'll do it later, not sure. See
this post
for the hue shifts I use to make the static battlers match.
I made an edit of the RTP imp sprite to match
Haydeos
's dark imp edit. There's also a matching face.
Spoiler:
Battlers
This is the matching enemy battler image for my inverted Suffering Soul (see the Sprites section). Front view version on the left, side view version on the right (the only difference is the eyes).
I decided to try removing the wings from the lamia battler, because I kinda prefer my lamia wingless. Front view version on the left, side view version on the right. (In addition to being flipped horizontally, the eyes are different.)
Spoiler:
Faces
To match my recoloured sprites, I recoloured the fairy face in 4 colours and also the fanatic, dark mage, and demon general faces. I also recoloured the assassin face. This one doesn't have a matching sprite because, being an assassin, he
ambushes
you and thus you never see him coming on the map. (It would probably be easy to do a matching sprite, I just didn't bother.) See
this post
for the hue shifts I use to make the static battlers match.
I made an edit of the RTP imp face to match
Haydeos
's dark imp edit. There's also a matching character sprite.
It barely qualifies, but I made a face graphic for the gargoyle. I just cropped it, scaled it up a bit, and slightly increased the contrast. It probably has plenty of room for improvement.
Spoiler:
Icons
These are random edits of RTP icons, mostly just recolours.
From left to right, top to bottom: quarterstaff, orb, firewood, blank, special sword, special pendant, special stone tablet, special stone, purple book, light blue book, crystal, black orb, green circle spell, light tornado, earth tornado, speech bubble.
These icons are made based on the hats of Actor2_5, Actor2_6, and Actor3_8. I made a colour version, a greyscale versions, and RTP-style versions in several colours.
If you use my
SFG_ExpandedTP
plugin and RTP icons, you might need these extra buff icons.
Spoiler:
Battle Animations
Seeing all those little chicks in the Garuda static battler, and the shadow bats in the Vampire battler, I thought – what if one or more of their attacks involve sending those little guys at you? So I decided to turn that into actual battle animations.
Unfortunately, this is something that's really not easy to show a screenshot of. To use them, simple download all the images and put them in your img/animations folder, then download the showcase project and copy-paste the animations from the database of the showcase project to the database of your real project.
The showcase project can only be downloaded
from my website
, as it's too large for an attachment. You can find the animation cell sheets below:

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I'm sorta wondering, has anyone ever shared battle animations? I mean, actually building the animation in the editor and passing along the Animations.json and possibly some animation sheets. I have a few I've made that I kinda like, though I wouldn't say they're super top-quality either…
Aside from that, I have a few more tile edits that I'm thinking of organizing and sharing soon, and I'm wondering whether it's even worth sharing sprite recolours that are just a hue shift that anyone could do.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Still debating the above questions (hoping someone will offer input on them), but… back on the topic of the altar, I decided to make a lit version of the chandelier. And then, I thought, why force all 3 candles to be lit at the same time? And then, I thought, why not allow removing the candles entirely? And then, I thought, what if you want your chandelier to not be gold? And then, since I used the RTP chandelier from !Flame, I thought I might as well apply all of those questions to that as well. And then I noticed that two of the wall sconces on !Flame don't have turned off versions, so I made one for them.
So now you can make a puzzle where you need to find the candles, insert them one by one (maybe in the correct order), and then light them one by one (maybe in the correct order).
See the opening post for all the details; I'll show just the empty ones here.
I'm not completely happy with the candelabrum recolours, but… I think they look passable. The lit sheet doesn't contain every possible combination, but it's easy to paste an empty candelabrum on top if the variation you want is missing.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
After spending a few hours recolouring some fairies, I decided to share them… and at the same time I thought I might as well share some of my other recolours.
The bats are extremely basic hue shifts that anyone could do in live 5 seconds, but I suppose maybe some people didn't think of it or don't even know how. I think the rat required some sort of tint or something, but it's been quite awhile since I did it, so I don't really remember.
The humanoid ones (including the fairies) were a bit more involved, because they required separating the sprite into different layers – as you can see, the face of the fanatic, dark mage, and assassin has not been recoloured. Similarly, for the fairies, while most of the various components
are
recoloured, it's not a single uniform hue shift.
The suffering soul is just a straight invert that probably anyone could do in like 5 seconds, but I thought it looked good and there was an extra slot on the sheet, so I threw it in.
I recoloured the faces for some of them too. No emotions though, sorry. There's also a random assassin face recolour with no matching sprite.
Also available are static battlers for the inverted Suffering Soul (see the opening post).
Spoiler:
Hue Shifts
For anyone interested, here are the hue shifts I use in the editor on the Enemy tab for the static battlers corresponding to the above sprites and faces:

Green Dark Mage: 192
Red-haired Fairy (fire): 306
Blue-haired Fairy (water): 180
Purple-haired Fairy (earth): 200
Green-haired Fairy (air): 68

did
make damage sprites for the recoloured fanatic and dark mage, so here they are.
LunarFlareStudios said:
I'm not sure that's even possible.
Click to expand...
...you don't think what's possible? Sharing animations? Why would it not be possible? Create a new blank project, quit the editor, replace the Animations.json file and add any needed images, add those images to your actual project too, open the blank project, select all the animations, open your real project, add enough spaces to fit the copied animations, select the blank spaces, and paste. I haven't actually tested, but… I think that should work? It's certainly quite non-trivial though. There's also the method of manually editing the Animations.json in your real project, pasting in the contents of the other Animations.json, and then opening it and resaving your project (to fix up the IDs), which would probably also work but is a little bit more error-prone.

posts.author: LunarFlareStudios
posts.body:
I'm not into coding, so I'm not exactly your go-to. I haven't used MV in a long time, though.
Try making a separate thread in General Resources (under the Resource Support thread), and see if anyone more skilled in coding is able to tell you if that's possible. I honestly don't think editing Animations.json will really work, but again, I know nothing about coding.
What I do know, however, is that it's not worth the risk if you're a novice at coding of any kind. One little typo can ruin everything.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: I am skilled in coding, and I'm confident it's possible – at most I missed a step or two in the above outline. The question was more along the lines of whether it may be worth sharing such animations at all.

posts.author: LunarFlareStudios
posts.body: Well, if that's the case, I think it's a bit easier to just post the resources/images... but I say at least try. I'm honestly not sure what the mods will think, but it's worth a shot.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: The images really aren't worth posting in isolation – I literally just cut-and-pasted bits from some static battlers into an animation cell sheet. It wasn't entirely trivial, admittedly, but anyone could've done it. They would've come up with something slightly different, but still. On the other hand, if it's accompanied by sample animations that actually use those cells, I thought it might be worth posting. The only issue is that, as mentioned in my earlier post, integrating posted animations into your project is quite a bit more work than just dropping in some images and using them.

posts.author: LunarFlareStudios
posts.body: People tend to like the easier way... but I'm interested in seeing what you came up with.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Alright! I've added them to a new section in the opening post. It's quite hard to show an actual screenshot of this in action, unfortunately – I could probably theoretically screenshot my game in the instant of the animation triggering, but that would be tough to time; or I could screenshot one frame in the animation editor; or I could show a video of one of the two; but none of those are easy to do.
I elected to provide a full project (but stripped down to the absolute minimum – the
only
resources in there are the SEs and the animation cell sheets) that you can copy-paste the animations from. Don't expect running the project to work – it'll probably crash because there's no window skin image or something. It's only intended as something to copy-paste from.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I needed some side stairs for the ramparts of my demon castle, so I made them. These match the castle roof in Outside_A4, and they expect to have a wall placed behind them. (You could try it without as well and just place shadows or something, not sure if that would look good.)
I also made some front-facing stairs for good measure; and there are some interior staircases there as well, matching the floor in Inside_A2 (though they don't directly match up like the outside stairs do).
Also added in the opening post is a few remixes of the quill and ink pot – see the post for more details.
Finally, I decided to try removing the wings from the Lamia battler, because I kinda prefer my lamias wingless. I'm not quite sure if this is done or if it needs a bit more touch-up. What do people think?

posts.author: LunarFlareStudios
posts.body: Never knew the Lamia even had wings. I guess I've been looking at it and I just never noticed. And yet I used MV for so long before switching to MZ...

Battle Animations
Seeing all those little chicks in the Garuda static battler, and the shadow bats in the Vampire battler, I thought – what if one or more of their attacks involve sending those little guys at you? So I decided to turn that into actual battle animations.
Unfortunately, this is something that's really not easy to show a screenshot of. To use them, simple download all the images and put them in your img/animations folder, then download the showcase project and copy-paste the animations from the database of the showcase project to the database of your real project.
